findings.severity: medium: before the warm-modern house, or any small-product layer, reaches a public build; noise in the flag build's control as soon as the phase-2 layers enter media/house
findings.what: The near-miss rule (dHash ≤ 48 and 32×32 grey MAD ≤ 3) matches near-blank images: 124 of our own warm-modern phase-2 layer and work files (75 shadow, 49 product) and the blank IMG1 canvas match products/floor-lamp-black-drum-linen-uaeow/opt-06334f443d (a thin floor lamp on white, mean ink 2.2), and so do white or transparent images. Placed as house layers in a public dist, 4 of them fail check:rights (exit 1). The public dist ships no media/house today, so today's public build passes.
findings.fix: Apply B only when both 32×32 images carry ink (mean of 255 − grey ≥ 4). Tested: story copies 321/321, true references 10/10, R7 and R16 kept; false positives 126 → 0. (A masked MAD gives the same numbers.) Keep printing the nearest non-supplier image per build: our nearest layer is 28 bits from rule A's 24.

findings.what: What the gate does not see (pixel study, 78 originals; and the CLI): a crop (0–2/78), padding onto a canvas (1/78), a border (1/78), a flip (0–2/78), a 3° rotation (2/78), a quarter-size JPEG (63/78); a hotlink to an image host no card names (ae-pic-a1.aliexpress-media.com, which appears 290k times in data/ but in no card); a data: URI split by CSS line continuations. The README names crop and flip only.
findings.fix: Cheap ones: also hash each supplier picture mirrored; trim white/transparent margins before hashing (padding, border, letterboxed social cards); a fixed base list of supplier image domains beside the cards' (alicdn.com, aliexpress-media.com, aliexpress.com, cjdropshipping.com, zendrop.com); remove CSS escapes and whitespace inside a data: URI before decoding. Any future image generator (social cards) writes its outputs to the ledger.

findings.what: The known-order strip has no word boundaries and adds the e-mail's domain parts as words, so it removes pieces of ordinary words and of our own fields: 'commit' → '[customer]mit', 'hotel' → 'ho[customer]', path '/complete' → '/[customer]plete', 'invalid' (from example.invalid). An error_id that contains a customer word of 3+ letters from its alphabet is mangled in the row (planted: E-DANA2345 → E-[customer]2345), so the id the customer quotes does not find the row.
findings.fix: Unicode word boundaries; never strip error_id, order_id, event or path; add only the e-mail's local part and the whole address, not its domain parts.

findings.what: errorCode still takes provider text through two doors: a non-own error's snake_case message prefix ('consignee_orna_rejected: …' → code 'consignee_orna_rejected') and a non-own error's name ('Orna' → error_name and code 'Orna'). Rows written with the plain logger (supplier.submit_failed, cancel.*, refund.*, notify.failed, shipment.sync_failed) do not get the known-order strip.
findings.fix: Message prefix and name only from our own classes (others: their HTTP status, a system code or 'Error'), or write those rows with orderLog.

findings.what: /healthz goes from degraded back to ok when a dead first claim is taken over and left to a person: degraded at T1+30.5 min, the takeover at T1+31 sets failing_since to now, and /healthz says 200 ok until about T1+61, while the order waits for a person.
findings.fix: On takeover set failing_since = COALESCE(failing_since, the dead claim's updated_at); or count supplier_error with reach 'maybe' as degraded at once.

findings.severity: low-medium: before HD_PUBLIC=1 with a real token
findings.owner: frontend-dev (the owner decides whether it matters)
findings.what: 'Not on the cart or the checkout' holds for a direct load only. On the site's own links the room, the product, the cart and the checkout are one document: the beacon loaded on the room keeps running while the customer types name, phone and address, under the room's CSP. (Cloudflare's script does not read forms as documented; spa:false should stop page views; both unverified here.)
findings.fix: Make the move into /checkout/ (and /cart/) a full page load, so those pages get their own document, no tag and their strict CSP; or accept it explicitly and say so in the runbook.

notes.what: ה3, negation: the brief's phrasings and the claims hold, but 10 of my 10 new denials still read 'הדפס במרקם' ('no embossed texture', 'no raised or embossed texture', 'neither textured nor embossed', 'isn't textured', 'texture: none', 'texture-free', 'no 3D texture', 'no visible texture', 'lacks texture', 'without embossed or textured finish'). No card says any of them today. Safer default: claim the texture only when no negation word is in the same clause, and list every 'הדפס במרקם' with its source text at build time.

An error of an unknown order outside production (preview, test, local) keeps the scrubbed message: a Latin name and a phone without its prefix ('54-771-6204') stay. By design; matters only if the preview environment ever sees real customers.

Confirmed frontend-dev's S18 item: under the delay line the order page still says 'אישור וחשבונית מס יישלחו לאימייל. נעדכן כשההזמנה יוצאת למשלוח.', and without a token 'את פרטי ההזמנה שלחנו לאימייל שלכם.'. No e-mail is sent today.
The delay line's live region is in the DOM 71–84 ms before its text. Correct in the DOM; not tested with a real screen reader (NVDA, VoiceOver).
AN1 assumptions to check in the Cloudflare dashboard after upload (runbook ch. 3 step 2): the 32-hex token format, spa:false, cookieless, the report on leaving the page.
IMG1 (README question 6): 42 pilot files, none matches a supplier picture (nearest real picture: our vase P2 at dHash 40, MAD 10.95). The gate will not block IMG1 images on today's numbers.
The near-miss rule is necessary, not cosmetic: it alone caught R7 (a half-size JPEG of a supplier photo, dHash 43), R16 (a 96 px inline copy, dHash 47) and 9 of the 321 story copies.
